items.title: Tennis star Taylor Fritz is selling his condo for $860,000—with sweeping views of Miami
items.description: Tennis star Taylor Fritz is serving up his Miami condo for $860,000, offering a buyer the chance to score a corner residence with sweeping views and a tennis court.

items.title: Tyler Perry cuts price of $36 million Wyoming property on 37 acres, buys $30 million Puerto Rico home
items.description: Tyler Perry has slashed $3.5 million from the asking price of his Wyoming mansion—days after picking up a $30 million home in Puerto Rico.

items.title: Musk says SpaceX landed a $40 billion debt deal — and forecasts doom for some AI rivals
items.description: SpaceX is rapidly growing an AI business that rents out access to advanced chips.

items.title: ‘She’s living the dream’: My stepmother said I can buy my childhood home for $850,000. Is she taking advantage of me?
items.description: “My late father bought our house for $250,000 in the 1990s.”

items.title: ‘I don’t feel sorry for myself’: I’m 64 and will be renting for the rest of my life. Is that so bad?
items.description: “I married a wonderful man with a good income. He left his job due to health issues and suffered a massive stroke at 53.”

items.title: We stopped helping our neighbors with free home repairs and our friendship cooled. Who’s to blame?
items.description: “Last summer, they complained about needing to replace their roof. A few months later, they bought a new SUV.”

items.title: My father-in-law, 81, sold his $75,000 home to pay his daughter’s $50,000 debt. How can I keep him from becoming destitute?
items.description: “Nothing has been set aside for his needs.”

items.title: My partner of 17 years left me his $1 million home. His children are livid. Am I obliged to split it with them?
items.description: “I never paid rent, although I put about $45,000 toward a new kitchen and a roof.”

items.title: We have a $300,000 mortgage with a 2.75% interest rate. I want to pay it off. My husband says I’m crazy. Who’s right?
items.description: “I don’t want to enter retirement owing six figures when we have the cash to clear it.”
